 Rounds of rain fuel weeklong flood threat along Florida Atlantic Coast ahead of possible move into Atlantic
 This flood threat has similar atmospheric conditions to the event that produced historic flooding in parts of Brevard County earlier this month.
 By
 Raymond Sanchez , Julian Atienza

 06:30 More rain fuels a flood threat for the East Coast of Florida 
 FOX Weather Correspondent Brandy Campbell continues her coverage from Melbourne, Florida, where residents are bracing for days of severe weather, including torrential rain, creating a serious flood threat.
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 Millions in Florida will be affected by periods of heavy rain and potential flash flooding through Saturday.
 This flood threat has similar atmospheric conditions to the event that produced historic flooding in parts of Brevard County earlier this month.
 The highest rain and storm chances are focused along the east coast of Florida, with the potential for widespread rain of 4 to 6 inches.
 These storms could move off the coast and strengthen into some kind of coastal storm by Saturday.
 JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — Millions of people along much of Florida 's Atlantic Coast will face a week-long flash flood threat that NOAA 's Weather Prediction Center (WPC) said has similar atmospheric conditions to the event that produced historic flooding in parts of Brevard County earlier this month .
 FLORIDA GOVERNOR DECLARES STATE OF EMERGENCY AS DEADLY FLOODING GRIPS SUNSHINE STATE 
 Florida rain setup
 (FOX Weather) 
 The WPC issued a Level 2 out of 4 flash flood risk from Jacksonville to Miami Tuesday, with rain already arriving over parts of North Florida.
 The FOX Forecast Center is tracking a weather disturbance that brought severe weather to Texas and Louisiana , which will move across the Gulf, but will get trapped over Florida for much of the week as easterly winds continuously funnel moisture over the region.
 WEST COAST BRACES FOR RELENTLESS BARRAGE OF STORMS AS POWERFUL ATMOSPHERIC RIVER FUELS HEAVY RAIN, STRONG SURF 
 That moisture will fuel periods of repeated downpours throughout the week.
 This graphic shows the prolonged flood threat for Florida.
 (FOX Weather) 
  Onshore winds are also expected to produce days of rough waves and dangerous rip currents .
 A high rip current risk is in effect for Melbourne , Stuart , Daytona Beach , Titusville , Fort Pierce and Vero Beach through Wednesday.
 This graphic shows the expected rainfall this week for Florida.
 (FOX Weather) 
  Repeated rounds of showers and occasional periods of heavy rain are enough to generate a Level 3 out of 4 flash flood threat from now through Friday, similar to the stretch of storms experienced around Halloween a few weeks ago.
 SUPER EL NIÑO DECLARED AS FORECASTERS WARN OF MAJOR SHIFTS IN WEATHER DURING WINTER SEASON 
 The high flash flood risk is in effect for the same areas impacted by historic flooding earlier this month. This includes Melbourne , which saw nearly a foot of rain in a single day, making it the city's rainiest day on record.
 This pattern of spiteful weather could last into the weekend, with the state stuck between high pressure in the north and moisture in the south, resulting in breezy, wet conditions.
 00:11 Florida Panthers fans slosh through flooded parking lot after game 
 Fans of the Florida Panthers had to trudge through heavy downpours and a flooded parking lot after a losing game to the Detroit Red Wings on Monday night.  
 The highest rain and storm chances are focused along Florida's east coast, with the potential for widespread rain of 4 to 6 inches throughout this week, with localized amounts surpassing 8 inches, according to the National Weather Service.
 MILLIONS ACROSS SOUTHEAST FACE POTENTIAL COASTAL STORM AS SOAKING RAIN AND GUSTY WINDS LOOM 
 According to the FOX Forecast Center , these storms could move off the coast and strengthen into some kind of coastal storm by Saturday.
 A Level 2 flash flood risk has been issued for parts of coastal South Carolina, Georgia and North Florida on Saturday.
 THANKSGIVING OUTLOOK: EL NIÑO-DRIVEN STORMS THREATEN TO WREAK HAVOC ON HOLIDAY TRAVEL FOR MILLIONS 
 "This system would bring strong winds and heavy rain up-and-down the Southeast coast leading up to the busy travel weekend," the FOX Forecast Center said.
 Check back for updates on this developing story.
